description: Rewrite notification.service.js to use the new grouped notification model with time-windowed grouping, push cooldowns, and smart socket updates. This replaces the existing per-event notification creation with group-based upserts.
steps: Step 1: Rewrite createNotification() in backend/src/modules/notifications/notification.service.js. The new logic: (a) Self-notification check remains (recipientId === senderId -> return null). (b) Load config via getNotificationConfig(). (c) For groupable types (Like, Save, Follow, Comment): calculate windowStart = new Date(Date.now() - config.groupingWindows[type]). Query NotificationGroup for an active group: {recipientId, type, targetId: postId||senderId, groupCreatedAt: {$gte: windowStart}}. If found: use findOneAndUpdate to $inc actorCount, $push recentActors (with $slice -maxRecentActors), set latestActivityAt=now, set isRead=false. If not found: create new NotificationGroup with actorCount:1, recentActors:[senderId], latestActivityAt:now, groupCreatedAt:now. (d) For AdminBroadcast/System: always create independent group (no aggregation). (e) After upsert/create: emit socket event NOTIFICATION_UPDATED (new event) with the full populated group data to allow client-side patching. Also emit NOTIFICATION_COUNT_CHANGED with fresh unread count from NotificationGroup.countDocuments({recipientId, isRead:false}). (f) Push cooldown logic: check lastPushSentAt on the group. If (now - lastPushSentAt) > config.pushCooldowns[type], send push and update lastPushSentAt. If within cooldown, skip push (socket + DB update still happen).

Step 2: Rewrite getUserNotifications() to query NotificationGroup instead of Notification. Populate recentActors with 'username avatarUrl'. Populate targetId conditionally - if targetType is 'Post', populate with 'media title'. Sort by latestActivityAt descending. Keep pagination, filter logic (all/unread/read), and unread count.
Step 3: Rewrite markAllAsRead() and markOneAsRead() to operate on NotificationGroup. Ensure markOneAsRead validates recipientId ownership.

Step 4: Update broadcastNotification() to create individual NotificationGroup documents (type: AdminBroadcast, targetType: System, actorCount: 0, recentActors: []) for each active user. Push sends immediately (cooldown = 0 for broadcasts). Keep BroadcastLog creation and push stats tracking exactly as-is.
Step 5: Add the new socket event to backend/src/realtime/events.js: NOTIFICATION_UPDATED: 'notification.updated'. Keep NOTIFICATION_COUNT_CHANGED as-is.

Step 6: Determine targetType and targetId mapping: For Like/Save/Comment -> targetType:'Post', targetId:postId. For Follow -> targetType:'User', targetId:senderId (the person being followed is the recipient, so targetId is who followed them - actually no, targetId should be the recipient's own ID or null... Let me reconsider. For Follow: the target is the user relationship itself. Set targetType:'User', targetId:null (since follows don't have a specific target entity other than the recipient). Actually the correct mapping for grouping Follow notifications is: targetType:null, targetId:null - group all follows to the same recipient within the window. This means all follows within 24h to user X become one group '5 people followed you'.

Step 7: Update the import in notification.service.js from './notification.model.js' (Notification) to also import from './notificationGroup.model.js' (NotificationGroup). Keep the old Notification import temporarily for backward compatibility during transition but do not create new documents in the old collection.
acceptance_criteria: createNotification() finds or creates a NotificationGroup within the configured time window
Repeated likes on the same post within 24h update the same group (increment actorCount, append to recentActors)
Repeated follows to the same user within 24h update the same group
After time window expires, a new group is created for subsequent activity
Push notifications respect cooldown - first activity sends push, subsequent within cooldown do not
AdminBroadcast creates individual groups per recipient with immediate push
Socket emits both NOTIFICATION_UPDATED (with group data) and NOTIFICATION_COUNT_CHANGED
getUserNotifications returns populated groups sorted by latestActivityAt
Unread count reflects number of unread groups, not individual events
